mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.15% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals economic weakness and reduced corporate earnings potential, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeds 0.5% and industrial production (INDPRO) growth falls below 0.2% in three months, it indicates labor market strain without output support, causing negative equity returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and INDPRO growth < 0.2% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and INDPRO growth < 0.2% in 3 months over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1100 units signals weakening consumer demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when HOUST falls below 1100 in late-cycle expansion regimes over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of retail sales (RSAFS) reflects strong consumer demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods when RSAFS exceeds the 90th percentile of its historical range over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 indicates a supply contraction, reducing corporate output and profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when INDPRO falls below 105.0 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) combined with stable federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive policy response, causing negative equity returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL growth > 0.3% and FEDFUNDS change <= 0.05% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL growth > 0.3% and FEDFUNDS change <= 0.05% in 3 months over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%), a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.15% triggers aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.5% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1% in 3 months
failure_condition: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%), SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1% in 3 months over any 3-year rolling window.
